The song was also composed and co-produced by [[the Invisible Men]] (Jason Pebworth, George Astasio and Jon Shave) and the Arcade (Kurtis Mckenzie).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pitchfork.com/news/53819-listen-iggy-azalea-featuring-charli-xcx-fancy/|title=Listen: Iggy Azalea Featuring Charli XCX "Fancy"|publisher=[[Pitchfork Media]]|date=7 February 2014}}</ref> The song is played in the key of [[C minor]] without any [[chord progression]] followed, and [[Charli XCX]]'s vocals range from G<sub>3</sub> to C<sub>5</sub>. It is in [[common time]] and is played at a [[tempo]] of 95 beats per minute.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.musicnotes.com/sheetmusic/mtdFPE.asp?ppn=MN0135428&ref=google|title=Iggy Azalea "Fancy" Sheet Music|date=21 May 2014 |publisher=musicnotes|access-date=31 May 2014}}</ref> The song features stabby synths and repeated [[hip hop]] chants of the word 'hey', which bear similarities to [[Mustard (record producer)|DJ Mustard's]] produced songs. Finger snaps are heard in the original mix.<ref name="popdust">{{cite web|author=Jacques Peterson |url=http://popdust.com/2014/02/06/listen-to-iggy-azalea-and-charli-xcxs-cocky-new-single-fancy/ |title=Listen To Iggy Azalea and Charli XCX's Cocky New Single, 'Fancy' |work=Popdust |date=29 September 2012 |access-date=13 April 2014}}</ref>

"Fancy" is a three-minute and 19-second electro-hop, electropop, and pop rap song, which was written by Iggy Azalea and Charli XCX. The song was also composed and co-produced by the Invisible Men (Jason Pebworth, George Astasio and Jon Shave) and the Arcade (Kurtis Mckenzie). The song is played in the key of C minor without any chord progression followed, and Charli XCX's vocals range from G<sub>3</sub> to C<sub>5</sub>. It is in common time and is played at a tempo of 95 beats per minute. The song features stabby synths and repeated hip hop chants of the word 'hey', which bear similarities to DJ Mustard's produced songs. Finger snaps are heard in the original mix.

After the song's premiere, it was revealed "Fancy" was the song that had leaked titled "Leave It".{{citation needed|date=April 2023}} On 17 February 2014, the song was serviced to [[urban contemporary]] radio in the United Kingdom as the album's fourth single.<ref name="autogenerated1">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/1xtra/playlist |title=BBC Radio 1xtra |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140204143220/http://www.bbc.co.uk/1xtra/playlist/ |archive-date=4 February 2014 |url-status=dead  }}</ref>
sections.text: On 5 December 2013, an unfinished song by Azalea, which surfaced with the title "Leave It", was leaked online. Azalea later revealed the song was produced by the Invisible Men and the Arcade, whom she collaborated with on her entire album. On 5 February 2014, Azalea announced that she would be releasing a new single titled "Fancy", featuring English singer-songwriter Charli XCX, later that week. The song was premiered on BBC Radio 1 Xtra the evening of 6 February 2014. After the song's premiere, it was revealed "Fancy" was the song that had leaked titled "Leave It".{{citation needed|date=April 2023}} On 17 February 2014, the song was serviced to urban contemporary radio in the United Kingdom as the album's fourth single.

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext:
[[File:Iggy Azalea - ACL Music Festival (6).jpg|thumb|left|270px|Azalea performing during the [[ACL Music Festival]] in November 2014]]
In the United States, "Fancy" has peaked at number one, becoming Azalea's first song to chart on the top of the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]]. The song is Charli XCX's second top 10 as a featured artist on the Hot 100 (the first being "[[I Love It (Icona Pop song)|I Love It]]") and her first number 1. On the issue date 17 May 2014 "Fancy" reached number two of the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Digital Songs]] chart, selling 222,000 units, occupying simultaneously the top two slots of the chart as "[[Problem (Ariana Grande song)|Problem]]" by [[Ariana Grande]], in which Azalea featured, debuted at the summit of Digital Songs chart. With this achievement, Azalea became only the sixth artist to occupy the top two position and the first to do so since [[Taylor Swift]] with the singles "[[We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together]]" and "[[Ronan (song)|Ronan]]" in 2012.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/6077608/frozen-spends-lucky-13th-week-at-no-1-lindsey-stirling-bows-at-no-2|last=Caulfield|first=Keith|title='Frozen' Spends Lucky 13th Week at No. 1, Lindsey Stirling Bows at No. 2|magazine=Billboard.com|date=7 May 2014|access-date=7 May 2014}}</ref> Azalea also became just the third female artist to place her first two Hot 100 hits in the top five simultaneously, first two being [[Ashanti (singer)|Ashanti]] and [[Mariah Carey]].<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Trust |first=Gary |url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/6077635/hot-100-john-legend-all-of-me-ariana-grande-iggy-azalea |title=John Legend's 'All of Me' Tops Hot 100, Ariana Grande Debuts at No. 3 |magazine=Billboard.com |access-date=7 May 2014}}</ref> It also marked Azalea as the first female rapper ever to have two songs concurrently in the top five of the Hot 100 chart.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/events/bbma-2014/6084776/ariana-grande-iggy-azalea-performers-billboard-music-awards |title= Ariana Grande, Iggy Azalea to Perform on 2014 Billboard Music Awards |magazine=Billboard |access-date=12 May 2014}}</ref> Moreover, Azalea passed [[Lil' Kim]] as the female rapper with the longest-leading number one on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/6143261/hot-100-iggy-azalea-fancy-magic-rude-shawn-mendes|title=Iggy Azalea Claims Longest Hot 100 Reign for a Female Rapper With 'Fancy'|magazine=Billboard|date= 2 July 2014}}</ref> and moved into a tie for fifth place among lead women who have scored the longest commands on the Hot 100 during the 2010s. The song led the chart for seven weeks, before being succeeded by [[Magic!|MAGIC]]'s "[[Rude (song)|Rude]]". "Fancy" remained in the top ten for 17 consecutive weeks.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/6150450/hot-100-iggy-azalea-fancy-maroon-5-maps|title=Iggy Azalea Tops Hot 100 For Seventh Week|magazine=Billboard|date= 9 July 2014}}</ref>

On the following week, Azalea became only the second artist in the nearly 10-year history of the Hot Digital Songs chart to have the top two songs concurrently for two weeks and, eventually, for three consecutive weeks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://music.yahoo.com/blogs/chart-watch/chart-watch-iggy-azalea-amazing-feat-215813622.html |title= Chart Watch: Iggy Azalea's Amazing Feat |date=14 May 2014 |publisher=Yahoo Music |access-date=15 May 2014}}</ref> On the week-ending 31 May 2014 the song ascended to number two on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100, selling 234,000 units, topped the [[Streaming Songs]] chart with 8.4 million impressions and continued to dominate the On-Demand Songs chart for a third week.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/6092276/michael-jackson-coldplay-hot-100-top-10-john-legend-no-1? |first=Gary|last=Trust|title=Michael Jackson, Coldplay Hit Hot 100's Top 10; John Legend Still No. 1|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |access-date=22 May 2014}}</ref> As it led the Streaming Songs chart for a thirteenth week it tied [[Miley Cyrus]]' "[[Wrecking Ball (Miley Cyrus song)|Wrecking Ball]]" for the most weeks tallied at number one.<ref>{{cite magazine|title=MAGIC! Still No. 1 on Hot 100 as Meghan Trainor & Charli XCX Soar|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/6214513/hot-100-magic-charli-xcx-meghan-trainor|magazine=Billboard |access-date=20 August 2014}}</ref> "Fancy" also reached number one on [[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'s [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs]] and [[Hot Rap Songs]], where it remained for 16 and 18 weeks respectively making it the longest running number one on these charts.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Ramirez |first=Rauly |url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/iggy-azaleas-fancy-hits-no-1-on-hot-rap-songs-chart/ |title=Iggy Azalea's 'Fancy' Hits No. 1 on Hot Rap Songs Chart |magazine=Billboard |access-date=25 April 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/biz/charts/2014-08-30/rap-song |title=Hot Rap Songs - Aug 30, 2014 - Billboard Chart Archive |magazine=Billboard |date= 30 August 2015}}</ref> Additionally, she is the first female Australian artist to top the Hot 100 since [[Olivia Newton-John]] reached the summit in 1981 with "[[Physical (Olivia Newton-John song)|Physical]]".<ref>{{cite web|last=Ryan|first=Gavin|url=https://www.noise11.com/news/justice-crew-spend-4th-week-on-top-of-aria-singles-20140531|title=Justice Crew Spend 4th Week on Top of ARIA Singles|publisher=Noise11. Noise Network|date=31 May 2014|access-date=2 June 2014}}</ref> Along with "[[Problem (Ariana Grande song)|Problem]]", Azalea has the distinction of being the first act to have its first two Hot 100-charting singles at numbers one and two at the same time since [[the Beatles]], as "Fancy" and "Problem" did, respectively.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/6099390/iggy-azalea-tops-hot-100-fancy-matches-beatles|magazine=Billboard|title=Iggy Azalea Tops Hot 100 With 'Fancy,' Matches Beatles' Historic Mark|first=Gary|last=Trust|date=28 May 2014|access-date=28 May 2014}}</ref> She is also only the second female artist to have the top 2 singles for multiple weeks, with the first being Ashanti.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/6106532/iggy-azalea-hot-100-fancy-magic-calvin-harris|magazine=Billboard|title=Iggy Azalea Remains Atop Hot 100 With 'Fancy'; MAGIC!, Calvin Harris Hit Top 10|first=Gary|last=Trust|date=4 June 2014|access-date=4 June 2014}}</ref> Azalea also became the fourth female rapper to top the [[Mainstream Top 40]] chart.<ref>{{cite 1s|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/chart-highlights-iggy-azalea-paramore-score-first-pop-radio-no/|magazine=Billboard |access-date=9 June 2014}}</ref> The song set new single-week records on [[Spotify]]'s U.S. streaming service for four consecutive weeks.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Maglio|first1=Tony|title=Iggy Azalea's 'Fancy' Tops 3 Million Spotify Streams for Fourth Straight Week|url=https://www.thewrap.com/iggy-azaleas-fancy-spotify-streams-record/|website=TheWrap.com|date=17 June 2014 |access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> On 3 September 2014, "Fancy" was named Billboard's top Song of the Summer for 2014 having led their weekly Songs of the Summer chart from start to finish.<ref name="bbsots">{{cite web|title=Iggy Azalea's 'Fancy' Is Billboard's Song of the Summer|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/iggy-azaleas-fancy-is-billboards-song-of-the-summer/|website=Billboard.com|access-date=3 September 2014}}</ref> "Fancy" was also named the most streamed song on Spotify in America in 2014.<ref>{{cite web|title=Iggy Azalea's "Fancy" Was The Most Streamed Song in America in 2014|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/hughmcintyre/2014/12/03/iggy-azaleas-fancy-was-the-most-streamed-song-in-america-in-2014/|website=Forbes.com|access-date=3 December 2014}}</ref> The song became the fifth best-selling song of 2014 in the United States with 3,970,000 copies sold for the year.<ref name="us sales 2014">{{cite web |url=http://www.nielsen.com/content/dam/corporate/us/en/public%20factsheets/Soundscan/nielsen-2014-year-end-music-report-us.pdf |title=Nielsen Music Report 2014 |date=7 January 2015 |publisher=Nielsen}}</ref> By 5 February 2015, the song had sold 4,100,000 copies.<ref name="fancysales">{{cite web |url=http://www.nielsen.com/us/en/insights/news/2015/early-winners-how-grammy-nominees-stack-up-before-musics-biggest-night.html |title=Early Winners: How GRAMMY Nominees Stack Up Before Music's |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150629183646/http://www.nielsen.com/us/en/insights/news/2015/early-winners-how-grammy-nominees-stack-up-before-musics-biggest-night.html |url-status=dead}}</ref>

In the United Kingdom, "Fancy" became her highest charting single as a lead artist at the time, debuting at number five on the [[UK Singles Chart]] and selling 38,320 copies in its first week.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Jones |first=Alan |url=http://www.musicweek.com/businessanalysis/read/official-charts-analysis-kaisers-enjoy-2nd-week-at-no-1/058191 |title=Official Charts Analysis: Kaisers enjoy 2nd week at No.1 |magazine=[[Music Week]] |access-date=14 April 2014}}</ref> In Australia, the song peaked at number five and has been certified quadruple platinum for sales of over 280,000 copies.<ref name="ARIA">{{cite web|url=http://www.ariacharts.com.au/chart/urban-singles|title=ARIA Australian Top 40 Urban Singles |publisher=Australian Recording Industry Association |date=4 May 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150510191204/http://www.ariacharts.com.au/chart/urban-singles |access-date=3 May 2015 |archive-date=10 May 2015 }}</ref> In its ninth week on the [[New Zealand Singles Chart]], the song climbed from number three to the top position,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://aotearoamusiccharts.co.nz/archive/singles/2014-05-09|title=NZ Top 40 Singles - The Official New Zealand Music Chart |publisher=[[Recorded Music NZ]]|date=9 May 2014}}</ref> giving Azalea her second number-one single there, after [[Ariana Grande]]'s "[[Problem (Ariana Grande song)|Problem]]", having replaced herself at the top, and first number-one there as a lead artist. In the United States, "Fancy" has peaked at number one, becoming Azalea's first song to chart on the top of the Billboard Hot 100. The song is Charli XCX's second top 10 as a featured artist on the Hot 100 (the first being "I Love It") and her first number 1. On the issue date 17 May 2014 "Fancy" reached number two of the Billboard Digital Songs chart, selling 222,000 units, occupying simultaneously the top two slots of the chart as "Problem" by Ariana Grande, in which Azalea featured, debuted at the summit of Digital Songs chart. With this achievement, Azalea became only the sixth artist to occupy the top two position and the first to do so since Taylor Swift with the singles "We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together" and "Ronan" in 2012. Azalea also became just the third female artist to place her first two Hot 100 hits in the top five simultaneously, first two being Ashanti and Mariah Carey. It also marked Azalea as the first female rapper ever to have two songs concurrently in the top five of the Hot 100 chart. Moreover, Azalea passed Lil' Kim as the female rapper with the longest-leading number one on the Billboard Hot 100 and moved into a tie for fifth place among lead women who have scored the longest commands on the Hot 100 during the 2010s. The song led the chart for seven weeks, before being succeeded by MAGIC's "Rude". "Fancy" remained in the top ten for 17 consecutive weeks.

On the following week, Azalea became only the second artist in the nearly 10-year history of the Hot Digital Songs chart to have the top two songs concurrently for two weeks and, eventually, for three consecutive weeks. On the week-ending 31 May 2014 the song ascended to number two on the Billboard Hot 100, selling 234,000 units, topped the Streaming Songs chart with 8.4 million impressions and continued to dominate the On-Demand Songs chart for a third week. As it led the Streaming Songs chart for a thirteenth week it tied Miley Cyrus' "Wrecking Ball" for the most weeks tallied at number one. "Fancy" also reached number one on Billboard's Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs and Hot Rap Songs, where it remained for 16 and 18 weeks respectively making it the longest running number one on these charts. Additionally, she is the first female Australian artist to top the Hot 100 since Olivia Newton-John reached the summit in 1981 with "Physical". Along with "Problem", Azalea has the distinction of being the first act to have its first two Hot 100-charting singles at numbers one and two at the same time since the Beatles, as "Fancy" and "Problem" did, respectively. She is also only the second female artist to have the top 2 singles for multiple weeks, with the first being Ashanti. Azalea also became the fourth female rapper to top the Mainstream Top 40 chart. The song set new single-week records on Spotify's U.S. streaming service for four consecutive weeks. On 3 September 2014, "Fancy" was named Billboard's top Song of the Summer for 2014 having led their weekly Songs of the Summer chart from start to finish. "Fancy" was also named the most streamed song on Spotify in America in 2014. The song became the fifth best-selling song of 2014 in the United States with 3,970,000 copies sold for the year. By 5 February 2015, the song had sold 4,100,000 copies.

In the United Kingdom, "Fancy" became her highest charting single as a lead artist at the time, debuting at number five on the UK Singles Chart and selling 38,320 copies in its first week. In Australia, the song peaked at number five and has been certified quadruple platinum for sales of over 280,000 copies. In its ninth week on the New Zealand Singles Chart, the song climbed from number three to the top position, giving Azalea her second number-one single there, after Ariana Grande's "Problem", having replaced herself at the top, and first number-one there as a lead artist. It also marks Charli XCX's second top-ten single, after Icona Pop's "I Love It", and first number-one single in New Zealand. It has also been certified double Platinum in New Zealand. The track had sold over 7 million copies worldwide, as of October 2014, making it one of the best-selling singles worldwide. On 23 December 2014, it was certified Triple Platinum in Canada after peaking at number one on the Canadian Hot 100, with 346,000 copies sold digitally throughout 2014. According to the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI), "Fancy" achieved combined sales and track-equivalent streams of 9.1 million units in 2014, ranking as the seventh best-selling single of the year.

Worldwidely, the song met a successful acclaim, especially in Europe where the song reached top twenty in several countries, such as Czech Republic, Finland and Ireland, top thirty in Belgium, Sweden, the Netherlands and France, top forty in Denmark, and top fifty in Austria, Switzerland and Slovakia. The song appeared equally in Germany, at number 51, becoming Azalea's first entry there and Charli XCX's second.

"Fancy" was first performed at the mtvU Woodie Awards during the SXSW Festival in Austin on 13 March 2014. Azalea and XCX also performed "Fancy" on Late Night with Seth Meyers on 17 March 2014. On 22 April 2014, the pair recreated the Clueless-inspired video once again during another televised live performance on Good Morning America for the release of Azalea's debut album The New Classic. They performed the song on Jimmy Kimmel Live on 16 May 2014, at the 2014 Billboard Music Awards on 18 May 2014 and on the season 18 finale of Dancing with the Stars on 20 May 2014. Azalea performed the song alone on the stage of the 2014 BET Awards on 29 June 2014 and at the 2014 ESPY Awards on 16 July 2014.

On 8 August 2014, Azalea performed "Fancy" on The Today Show as part of the Toyota concert series in Rockefeller Center, New York City. The song was also included in the setlist of her 2014 The New Classic Tour of North America and Europe, and also XCX's 2014 Girl Power North America Tour. The track was included on Azalea's medley performances on Saturday Night Live on 25 October 2014, and at the 2014 American Music Awards on 23 November 2014, with XCX joining her on stage for the latter. On 31 December 2014, Azalea and XCX performed the song on Dick Clark's New Year's Rockin' Eve.
